strings.title: Packs of Juice Boxes
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: A rate stays the same in every row: 1 pack has 6 juice boxes, so build up with rows you know (2 packs, 5 packs, 10 packs) to find any number of packs.
strings.keywords: rate, for every, per, ratio table, times as many, packs, boxes
watchFor: Adding the same amount to both columns (1:6 to 2:7): ask "If 1 pack has 6, how many do 2 packs have?"
Starting from 1 pack every time: ask "Is there a row in the table that helps?"
Going backward (42 boxes) feels hard: ask "How many packs make 42? Which row is close?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Which rows were the most useful?" Land: 1, 5 and 10 are friendly rows; add or double rows to get the rest. The rate (6 per pack) stays the same in every row.

problems.notes: Context: "One pack has 6 juice boxes. How many in 2 packs?" Look for: double 6. Ask: "How many boxes in 2 packs?" Word choice: "6 boxes per pack". Model: ratio packs:boxes, 1:6, 2:12

responses.tip: Added 1 to each side. Ask: does the second pack have only 1 box?

problems.notes: Context: "How many in 5 packs?" Look for: half of 10 packs, or 5 sixes. Ask: "Which row is easy to find?" Model: ratio packs:boxes, 1:6, 10:60, 5:30

responses.say: 10 packs is 60, so 5 packs is half: 30.

problems.notes: Context: "How many in 10 packs?" Look for: double 5 packs, or 10 sixes. Ask: "How does the last row help?" Model: ratio packs:boxes, 1:6, 5:30, 10:60
Context: "How many in 15 packs?" Look for: 10 packs + 5 packs = 60 + 30. Ask: "Which two rows add to 15 packs?" Model: ratio packs:boxes, 10:60, 5:30, 15:90

responses.tip: Added 1 pack, not 5. Ask: 10 packs plus how many packs make 15?

problems.notes: Context: "How many in 20 packs?" Look for: double 10 packs. Ask: "What's the quickest row to use?" Model: ratio packs:boxes, 1:6, 10:60, 20:120
Context: "We need 42 juice boxes. How many packs?" Look for: 5 packs is 30, 2 packs is 12, so 7 packs. Ask: "Which rows add to 42 boxes?" Model: ratio packs:boxes, 5:30, 2:12, 7:42

responses.say: 5 packs is 30 and 2 packs is 12. 7 packs.

responses.tip: Ask: we know the boxes. What are we looking for?

problems.notes: Context: "How many in 8 packs?" Look for: 10 packs take away 2 packs, or double, double, double. Ask: "Who used a different row?" Model: ratio packs:boxes, 10:60, 2:12, 8:48

strings.title: Legs and Wheels
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: A rate is the same in every row: every dog has 4 legs. Build up from rows you know, and work backward to find how many dogs.
strings.keywords: rate, for every, each, per, ratio table, times as many
watchFor: Adding 4 instead of multiplying (3 dogs have 7 legs): ask "How many legs does each dog have?"
Stuck going backward (36 legs): ask "How many 4s in 36?"
Starting from 1 every time: ask "Which row in the table helps?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "How did the table help you go backward?" Land: the rate stays the same, so the table works both ways. To find dogs from legs, ask how many 4s are in the number of legs.

problems.notes: Context: "Every dog has 4 legs. How many legs on 3 dogs?" Look for: 3 groups of 4. Ask: "Hold on to this." Word choice: "4 legs per dog". Model: ratio dogs:legs, 1:4, 3:12

responses.tip: Ask: how many legs does each dog have?

problems.notes: Context: "6 dogs?" Look for: double 3 dogs. Ask: "How does the last row help?" Model: ratio dogs:legs, 3:12, 6:24
Context: "10 dogs?" Look for: 40. Ask: "What's a friendly row?" Model: ratio dogs:legs, 1:4, 10:40
Context: "12 dogs?" Look for: 10 dogs + 2 dogs. Ask: "Which rows add to 12?" Model: ratio dogs:legs, 10:40, 2:8, 12:48
Context: "There are 36 legs. How many dogs?" Look for: how many 4s in 36. Ask: "Which row is close?" Model: ratio dogs:legs, 10:40, 1:4, 9:36

responses.say: 10 dogs is 40 legs, one less dog: 9.

responses.tip: Ask: we know the legs. What are we looking for?

problems.notes: Context: "Every tricycle has 3 wheels. How many wheels on 7 tricycles?" Look for: a new rate. Ask: "What changed?" Model: ratio trikes:wheels, 1:3, 7:21
Context: "60 wheels. How many tricycles?" Look for: 10 trikes is 30, so 20 is 60. Ask: "Which row helps?" Model: ratio trikes:wheels, 10:30, 20:60
